character: Bumpy, abrasive former WWII airfield circuit in Florida — one of the roughest surfaces in racing, mixing concrete runway sections with tarmac. Precision over the bumps and a strong exit from the final corner define the lap.

corners.name: Turn 1
corners.type: heavy-braking corner off the front straight
corners.technique: Brake hard over the bumpy surface, late apex
corners.trap: The bumps under braking make lockups common

corners.name: Hairpin
corners.type: tight, slow-speed corner (Turn 7) with a notoriously bumpy braking zone
corners.technique: Precision braking over the bumps, smooth throttle application
corners.trap: The bumpy surface unsettles the car right at the braking point

corners.name: Sunset Bend
corners.type: fast, bumpy right-hander onto the front straight (Turn 17)
corners.technique: Commit through the bumps — tight on exit if taken correctly
corners.trap: Heavy braking zone with varying racing lines makes this the corner Sebring is best known for
